chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me, who said: Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to me from 'Amr ibn Uthman from Ahmad ibn Ismail al-Katib who said:

Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) entered the Masjid al-Haram, and a group of Quraish looked at him and said: 'This is the god of the people of Iraq.' Some of them said: 'Send one of you to ask him.' A young man came to him and asked: 'O Uncle, what is the greatest of the major sins?' He replied: 'Drinking wine.' He went to them and informed them. They told him: 'Go back to him.' They did not cease urging him until he returned to him and asked him again. He said to him: 'Did I not tell you, O nephew, that drinking wine is [the greatest sin]? Indeed, drinking wine leads its drinker into adultery, theft, and killing of the soul whom Allah has forbidden except by right, and into polytheism. By Allah, the deeds of wine rise above every sin just as its tree rises above every tree.'
ai.seo_question: What is the greatest major sin according to Imam Muhammad ibn Ali (peace be upon him) and why?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this narration highlights the Imam's authority in defining spiritual hierarchy, identifying alcohol not merely as a vice but as the root cause of other major sins. The metaphor of the tree towering over others underscores the Shia scholarly view of *khamr* as a comprehensive gateway to moral decay, linking physical intoxication to spiritual polytheism (*shirk*) and legal transgressions like theft and murder.
